criterion: Both are pinned by a named test and a mutation-audit entry, and the guard count in any claim is measured rather than stated
summary: Count claim accurate: len(GUARDS) == 41, all 41 names unique, and the full audit's own summary says 41 of 41 - two independent measurements agreeing with the claim, and exactly four prefixed 'doctor:'. Both audit runs quoted verbatim. Reviewer did not take the audit's credit on trust: it applied all four mutations by hand in copies, asserting each old string occurs exactly once, and reported the exact failure text for each. On the specific concern raised, the `if True:` mutant fails on the assertion rather than producing unasserted warnings, because the test ends by comparing the filtered warning list against the empty list. IT ALSO CORRECTED THE EXECUTOR IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION: the claim that two of its own tests were vacuous is itself imprecise. The reviewer built a fifth tree reverting the whole block to the real pre-fix read_text and ran the pipe test, which failed with subprocess.TimeoutExpired in 60.18s - so that test does distinguish HEAD from the code that actually shipped, and is not vacuous in the plain sense. It cannot distinguish HEAD from a non-blocking plain os.open, which is the narrower true statement the guard comment makes immediately above its overstated closing line. Judged a wording imprecision rather than a misleading guard. Gates: 424 tests OK on both interpreters with all six new tests running rather than skipped on 3.10; black, mypy and sync_adapters clean; graphctl validate true.
